description: Adversarial per-fact retention controls constructed before tail-replacement trials. Each asks for ten facts under an eight-record budget; total completion is impossible and excluded from recall headlines. Detect replacing one supplied fact with another, even when aggregate supplied counts stay equal.

corpus.title: Shared memory store
corpus.content: Share a SQLite connection behind a lock so concurrent memory callers use one store.

corpus.title: Retrieval query
corpus.content: A lookup carries a repository, task, optional failure and file paths, a result limit, verification filters and excluded tags.

corpus.title: Memory record
corpus.content: Keep trust, applicability, provenance, repository, claim text and its hash together.

corpus.title: Workload status
corpus.content: Expose automatic and maximum slots, busy and waiting commands, processor count and available memory.

corpus.title: Browser proxy
corpus.content: Keep the browser proxy server and optional credentials together; direct mode uses direct://.

corpus.title: Command output
corpus.content: An absent exit code means a signal or timeout; retain stdout, stderr, stop state and truncated-output metadata.

corpus.title: Process tree
corpus.content: On Windows use a job object to end a spawned shell and its descendants together, falling back to tree termination when no job can be made.

corpus.title: Browser screenshot
corpus.content: Keep the URL, page title, image dimensions and attachment identifier; encode image bytes only when building a vision request.

corpus.title: Telemetry notes
corpus.content: Telemetry measures response latency and counts completed observations.

corpus.title: Allocation notes
corpus.content: Allocation records track released buffers and allocation totals.

corpus.title: File context
corpus.content: This file only configures logging destinations.
